steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with the molecules in Earth's atmosphere. Shorter wavelengths of visible light — particularly blue light — are scattered much more efficiently than longer wavelengths like red and orange, causing blue light to be redirected in all directions across the sky. When you look up, your eyes receive this scattered blue light from all parts of the sky, making it appear blue, while colors like red are less scattered and remain more concentrated near the horizon (which is why sunsets often appear red and orange).

---
